entry.pre_arrival: None today. ETIAS is on the watch list.
entry.other: Greenland and the Faroe Islands are outside Schengen and the EU, with their own visa-free entry for visa-free nationalities. Schengen Entry/Exit System: fingerprints and photo at the border on first entry (free, nothing to do beforehand). Get an entry stamp where one is still given, and carry your passport across internal borders.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The currency is the Danish Krone (DKK). If you travel between Denmark and any non-EU country, you must declare cash of over 10,000 euros (or equivalent). This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. If you don't declare or give the wrong information on entry or exit, you'll need to pay a fine. You don't need to declare cash if you're travelling to or from another EU country. ATMs are common, and credit cards are accepted in most places. Check if your credit card has 'chip and PIN' technology. Many hotels, restaurants and shops need this.

laws.rule: It's illegal to wear clothing which covers the face while in a public place. You'll be fined if you don't comply, and the fine increases for repeat offenders. The law applies to both residents and visitors. Penalties for vandalism, such as graffiti, may include fines, jail and/or deportation. Contact the Danish Civil Aviation and Railway Authority for more information and guidance on registration. Holders of Australian superannuation accounts should seek advice on taxation before moving to Denmark.

visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Visa-free short stays (90 days or less) as part of the Schengen area, in some cases.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Nothing to lodge before travel today: EES registration happens at the border. ETIAS hadn't started on 2026-11-01.
steps: Denmark is in the Schengen area: short stays of 90 days or less can be visa-free in some cases; other purposes or longer stays need a visa before travel.
At the first Schengen border, give fingerprints and a photo for the Entry/Exit System (EES). It's free; nothing is needed before arrival, and sites charging for it are fraudulent.
Carry your passport when crossing borders, including inside Schengen (temporary internal checks are in place in places).
Greenland and the Faroe Islands aren't in Schengen or the EU.
